title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice on Issuing the Opinions on Further Strictly Handling Cases in Accordance with the Law to Ensure the Quality of Death Penalty Case Adjudication
keywords_en: Guarantee; Handling cases according to law to ensure proper handling of death penalty cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate
Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issuing the "Opinions on Further Strictly Handling Cases According to Law and Ensuring the Quality of Handling Death Penalty Cases"

Fa Fa [2007] No. 11

To the Higher People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), and Justice Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army, the Security Department of the General Political Department; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, the Public Security Bureau, and the Justice Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The "Opinions on Further Strictly Handling Cases According to Law and Ensuring the Quality of Handling Death Penalty Cases" are hereby issued to you for earnest implementation. Please report any issues encountered during implementation and any problems to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice in a timely manner.

March 9, 2007

Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Justice

Opinions on Further Strictly Handling Cases According to Law and Ensuring the Quality of Handling Death Penalty Cases

The Central Committee has decided to reform the practice of authorizing higher people's courts to exercise the power to approve the death penalty for certain categories of cases, and to centralize the power of death penalty approval in the Supreme People's Court. This reform requires strict adherence to legal procedures in handling cases to ensure the quality of death penalty case processing. On October 31, 2006, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress adopted the "Decision on Amending the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China," deciding that from January 1, 2007, the Supreme People's Court would uniformly exercise the power to approve death penalty cases. In order to conscientiously implement this major decision and deployment of the Central Committee, the following opinions are hereby put forward regarding the strict handling of death penalty cases according to law by people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs:

I. Fully Recognize the Significant Importance of Ensuring the Quality of Handling Death Penalty Cases

1. The death penalty is the most severe punishment, depriving a criminal of life. The Central Committee's decision to centralize the power of death penalty approval in the Supreme People's Court is a major measure to build a socialist harmonious society, implement the basic strategy of governing the country according to law, and respect and safeguard human rights. It is conducive to maintaining social and political stability, promoting the uniformity of the national legal system, and systemically ensuring the prudence and fairness of death penalty judgments. It is of great significance for guaranteeing fairness and justice throughout society, consolidating the people's democratic dictatorship, and building a moderately prosperous society in all respects.

2. The uniform exercise of the power to approve death penalty cases by the Supreme People's Court imposes new and higher requirements on the work of people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs. Case handling quality is the lifeline of the work of people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs. In death penalty cases, where human lives are at stake, quality is particularly important. Ensuring the quality of handling death penalty cases is the key to the smooth implementation of this major decision of the Central Committee and is also the most fundamental requirement. People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs at all levels must attach great importance, unify their thinking, raise awareness, align their actions with the Central Committee's decision, adhere to the guidance of Deng Xiaoping Theory and the important thought of the "Three Represents," fully implement the Scientific Outlook on Development, firmly establish the socialist concept of the rule of law, perform their duties according to law, strictly implement the Criminal Law and the Criminal Procedure Law, and strictly control the factual basis, evidence, procedures, and application of law in death penalty cases, so that every death penalty case handled can withstand the test of history.

II. Principles and Requirements to Be Followed in Handling Death Penalty Cases

(1) Combining Punishment of Crime with Protection of Human Rights

3. China is currently in an important period of strategic opportunities for comprehensively building a moderately prosperous society and accelerating socialist modernization. At the same time, it is a period of prominent contradictions among the people, high incidence of criminal offenses, and complex struggles against enemies. The task of maintaining social harmony and stability is quite heavy. It is necessary to continue adhering to the policy of "striking hard" (yanda), correctly use the death penalty as a means of punishment to combat serious criminal offenses, and effectively curb the rampant and spreading momentum of criminal activities. At the same time, the constitutional principle of "the state respects and safeguards human rights" must be fully implemented, and the legitimate rights and interests of criminal suspects and defendants must be effectively protected. Adhere to the equal emphasis on punishing crimes according to law and protecting human rights according to law; adhere to the basic principles of legality, proportionality of crime and punishment, equality of all persons before the criminal law, open trial, and statutory procedures; truly achieve that those who commit crimes are punished according to law, and those who are innocent are not criminally prosecuted.

(2) Adhere to the Retention of the Death Penalty, Strictly Control and Cautiously Apply the Death Penalty

4. "Retain the death penalty, strictly control the death penalty" is China's basic death penalty policy. Practice has proven that this policy is completely correct and must continue to be implemented. It is necessary to fully and accurately understand and implement the "strike hard" policy, severely punish serious criminal offenses according to law, and resolutely impose the death penalty according to law on the extremely few criminals whose crimes are extremely serious. China cannot abolish the death penalty at present, but its application should be gradually reduced. Those who could be executed or not should absolutely not be executed. When handling death penalty cases, it is necessary, in accordance with the requirements of building a socialist harmonious society and maintaining social stability, to be rigorous and prudent. While ensuring the correct determination of case facts based on evidence and preventing the occurrence of wrongful convictions, it is also necessary to ensure accurate conviction and appropriate sentencing, achieving the principle of executing fewer and with caution.

(3) Adhere to Equal Emphasis on Procedural Justice and Substantive Justice, Protect the Legitimate Rights of Criminal Suspects and Defendants

5. When people's courts, people's procuratorates, and public security organs conduct criminal proceedings, they must not only ensure the correctness of substantive case handling but also ensure the legitimacy and legality of the criminal procedure itself. At all stages of investigation, prosecution, and trial, they must always insist on proceeding according to law, resolutely overcome the erroneous concepts of emphasizing substance over procedure and emphasizing suppression over protection, respect the litigation status of criminal suspects and defendants, and effectively protect the full exercise of the right to defense and other litigation rights by criminal suspects and defendants, avoiding the occurrence of wrongful convictions due to the deprivation or restriction of the legitimate rights of criminal suspects and defendants.

(4) Adhere to the Principle of Evidence-Based Adjudication, Emphasize Evidence, and Do Not Lightly Rely on Confessions

6. When handling death penalty cases, adhere to the principle of emphasizing evidence and not lightly relying on confessions. If there is only the defendant's confession and no other evidence, the defendant cannot be found guilty; if there is no defendant's confession but other evidence is reliable and sufficient, the defendant may be found guilty. Confessions of criminal suspects or defendants obtained through torture, and victim statements or witness testimony obtained through violence, threats, or other illegal methods, cannot be used as the basis for deciding a case. For cases where the defendant is found guilty, it must strictly comply with Article 162 of the Criminal Procedure Law, achieving "clear facts, reliable and sufficient evidence." If the evidence is insufficient and the defendant cannot be found guilty, a verdict of not guilty due to insufficient evidence and unestablished charges should be rendered.

(5) Adhere to the Criminal Policy of Combining Leniency with Severity

7. When applying punishment in death penalty cases, it is necessary to prevent both heavy sentences for minor crimes and light sentences for serious crimes, achieving proportionality between crime and punishment, appropriate punishment for the crime, heavy punishment for serious crimes, light punishment for minor crimes, and no punishment for the innocent. Defendants whose crimes are extremely serious must be punished and severely cracked down upon according to law; defendants who have statutory circumstances for "shall" be given a lighter, mitigated, or exempted punishment shall be treated leniently according to law; defendants who have statutory circumstances for "may" be given a lighter, mitigated, or exempted punishment shall, in principle, be treated leniently according to law unless there are other special circumstances; defendants with discretionary circumstances for lenient punishment shall also be considered according to law.

III. Conscientiously Perform Statutory Duties, Strictly Handle Death Penalty Cases According to Law

(1) Investigation

8. Investigative organs shall, in accordance with the procedures stipulated by the Criminal Procedure Law, judicial interpretations, and other relevant regulations, comprehensively and promptly collect various evidence proving whether the criminal suspect is guilty or innocent, or the severity of the crime, involving all facts of the case; illegal collection of evidence is strictly prohibited.

9. For criminal suspects who may be mentally ill, minors, or pregnant women, timely identification or investigation and verification shall be conducted.

10. Strengthen the collection, preservation, and fixation of evidence. The original items and original documents of evidence shall be properly preserved and shall not be damaged, lost, or disposed of without authorization. Items, documents, electronic data, traces, persons, corpses, etc., related to the facts of the case that require identification shall be promptly subjected to criminal science and technology identification, and the identification report shall be attached to the case file. In cases involving homicide, the identity of the victim shall be determined through identification by close relatives of the victim, DNA identification, fingerprint identification, and other methods. Biological evidence, traces, items such as bloodstains, seminal stains, hair, fingerprints, etc., left at the scene related to the crime that have conditions for identical identification examination shall be subjected to identical identification with the corresponding biological samples, biological characteristics, items, etc., of the criminal suspect through criminal science and technology identification methods such as DNA identification and fingerprint identification. The investigative organ shall inform the criminal suspect and the victim of the identification conclusions used as evidence. If the criminal suspect or victim applies, supplementary identification or re-identification may be conducted.

11. Interrogation of criminal suspects in custody shall be conducted in the detention center where the criminal suspect is held. Torture to obtain confessions or other illegal methods to obtain statements are strictly prohibited. When interrogating a criminal suspect, in addition to making a written record, audio or video recording may be made as needed.

12. Investigators questioning witnesses or victims shall be conducted in accordance with Article 97 of the Criminal Procedure Law. Illegal evidence collection and violent evidence collection are strictly prohibited.

13. After the first interrogation by the investigative organ or from the date of the adoption of compulsory measures, if the criminal suspect hires a lawyer or is assigned a lawyer by a legal aid institution to provide legal consultation, represent the lodging of complaints or accusations, the investigative organ shall ensure that the lawyer exercises rights and performs duties according to law. If the case involves state secrets, the criminal suspect's hiring of a lawyer or application for legal aid, and the lawyer's meeting with the criminal suspect in custody, shall be approved by the investigative organ. If the lawyer discovers instances of torture, he or she may report to the public security organ or the people's procuratorate.

14. When the investigative organ transfers a case to the people's procuratorate for review and prosecution, it shall transfer all evidence related to the facts of the case, including the first interrogation record and records of inquests, examinations, and searches, proving whether the criminal suspect is guilty or innocent, or the severity of the crime.

15. For cases in which the death penalty may be imposed, the people's procuratorate shall comprehensively and objectively review evidence during the review of arrest. Confessions of criminal suspects, victim statements, and witness testimony obtained through illegal methods such as torture shall be excluded according to law. Corrective opinions shall be raised regarding illegal activities in investigative operations.

(2) Initiation of Public Prosecution

16. The people's procuratorate shall perform its duties of reviewing prosecution according to law and strictly adhere to the statutory standards for initiating prosecution.

17. Within three days of receiving the case materials transferred for review and prosecution, the people's procuratorate shall inform the criminal suspect of the right to entrust a defender; if the criminal suspect is financially distressed, it shall inform him or her of the right to apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution. From the date of review and prosecution, defense lawyers may consult, extract, and copy the litigation documents and technical identification materials of the case, and may meet and correspond with the criminal suspect in custody. Other defenders, with the permission of the people's procuratorate, may also consult, extract, and copy the above materials and meet and correspond with the criminal suspect in custody. The people's procuratorate shall facilitate defenders in consulting, extracting, and copying materials.

18. When reviewing a case, the people's procuratorate shall interrogate the criminal suspect, hear the opinions of the victim and the persons entrusted by the criminal suspect and the victim, and make a record attached to the case file. If the victim and the persons entrusted by the criminal suspect and the victim have not submitted opinions during the review and prosecution period, this shall be noted and attached to the file. If the people's procuratorate has doubts about the record of witness testimony or considers the questioning of the witness to be insufficient or incomplete, it may question the witness and make a record.

19. When interrogating the criminal suspect, the people's procuratorate shall listen to both the guilty confession and the innocent or mitigated-defense statements of the criminal suspect. If the criminal suspect claims to have been subjected to torture, the people's procuratorate may require the investigators to provide an explanation, and if necessary, conduct verification. Confessions of criminal suspects obtained through torture, and victim statements or witness testimony obtained through violence, threats, or other illegal methods, shall not be used as the basis for prosecuting the crime.

20. For criminal suspects who may be mentally ill, minors, or pregnant women, timely appointment of identification or investigation and verification shall be conducted.

21. When reviewing a case, if the people's procuratorate considers that a re-inquest or re-examination of the public security organ's inquest or examination is necessary, it shall request the public security organ to conduct a re-inquest or re-examination, and the people's procuratorate may send personnel to participate; the people's procuratorate may also conduct the re-inquest or re-examination itself, and may consult with the public security organ to send personnel to participate, and if necessary, it may hire specialized technical personnel to participate.

22. If the people's procuratorate has doubts about physical evidence, documentary evidence, audio-visual materials, or records of inquests or examinations, it may request investigators to provide relevant information on their acquisition or production. If necessary, it may question the persons who provided the physical evidence, documentary evidence, or audio-visual materials, and commission technical identification of the physical evidence, documentary evidence, or audio-visual materials. The circumstances of the questioning and identification shall be attached to the file.

23. When reviewing a case, if the people's procuratorate considers that the facts are unclear, the evidence insufficient, or that there are omitted crimes or omitted co-defendants, and supplementary investigation is required, it shall provide specific opinions on the required supplementary investigation and return the case materials to the public security organ for supplementary investigation. The public security organ shall complete the supplementary investigation within one month. The people's procuratorate may also conduct the investigation itself, and if necessary, request assistance from the public security organ.

24. After reviewing a case, if the people's procuratorate considers that the facts of the criminal suspect's crime have been clearly ascertained, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, and criminal responsibility should be pursued according to law, it shall make a decision to initiate prosecution. Under any of the following circumstances, it may be confirmed that the facts of the crime have been clearly ascertained: (1) In cases involving a single crime, the facts ascertained are sufficient for conviction and sentencing, or the facts related to conviction and sentencing have been ascertained, and the facts that do not affect conviction and sentencing cannot be ascertained; (2) In cases involving multiple crimes, some crimes have been ascertained and meet the conditions for prosecution, while other crimes cannot be ascertained; (3) The tools used to commit the crime cannot be recovered or the whereabouts of the stolen goods are unknown, but other evidence is sufficient for conviction and sentencing of the criminal suspect; (4) The main facts in the testimony of witnesses, the confessions and defenses of the criminal suspect, and the statements of the victim are consistent, with only minor inconsistencies that do not affect conviction. For situations falling under item (2), prosecution shall be initiated based on the crimes that have been ascertained.

25. After reviewing a case returned for supplementary investigation, if the people's procuratorate still considers that the conditions for prosecution are not met, it may make a decision not to prosecute. Under any of the following circumstances, where it cannot be determined that the criminal suspect constitutes a crime and criminal responsibility must be pursued, this constitutes insufficient evidence and does not meet the conditions for prosecution: (1) The evidence used for conviction is in doubt and cannot be verified; (2) There is a lack of necessary evidence to prove the facts constituting the elements of the crime; (3) The contradictions in the evidence used for conviction cannot be reasonably excluded; (4) The conclusions drawn from the evidence have other possibilities.

26. If the people's court considers that the relevant materials transferred by the people's procuratorate for prosecution do not meet the conditions specified in Article 150 of the Criminal Procedure Law and submits a written opinion to the people's procuratorate requesting supplementary provision, the people's procuratorate shall provide the supplementary materials within three days of receiving the notice. If it cannot provide them within the time limit, the people's procuratorate shall provide a written explanation.

(3) Defense and Provision of Legal Assistance

27. Lawyers shall abide by professional ethics and practice discipline, and when handling death penalty cases, they shall perform their duties diligently, carrying out work such as meetings, reviewing files, investigating and collecting evidence, and appearing in court for defense, improving the quality of defense, and effectively safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of criminal suspects and defendants.

28. With the consent of witnesses or other relevant units or individuals, defense lawyers may collect evidence proving that the criminal suspect or defendant is innocent or has a minor crime; they may apply to the people's procuratorate or the people's court to collect or obtain evidence, or apply to the people's court to notify a witness to appear in court to testify; they may also apply to the people's procuratorate or the people's court to entrust an identification institution to conduct supplementary identification or re-identification of disputed identification conclusions. The people's procuratorate or the people's court shall promptly respond to the above applications of the defense lawyer.

29. If a defendant may be sentenced to death without retaining a defender, the people's court shall, through a legal aid institution, designate a lawyer who undertakes legal aid obligations to provide defense. The legal aid institution shall, within three days of receiving the notice of designated defense, assign a lawyer with experience in criminal defense to provide defense.

30. If lawyers encounter difficulties or problems in providing legal assistance or performing defense duties, the judicial administrative organs shall promptly coordinate with the public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts to resolve them, ensuring that lawyers perform their duties according to law.

(4) Trial

31. After accepting a case, the people's court shall inform the victim who has suffered material losses due to the criminal act, the close relatives of the deceased victim, or the legal representatives of victims without capacity or with limited capacity, that they have the right to file an incidental civil action and to entrust an agent ad litem. If they are financially distressed, they shall also be informed that they may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution. During the trial process, emphasis shall be placed on the important role of civil mediation in incidental civil actions, and efforts shall be made to appease victims and their close relatives, effectively strengthening the protection of the rights and interests of criminal victims.

32. The people's court shall notify the following categories of victims, witnesses, and expert witnesses to appear in court to testify: (1) Where the people's procuratorate, the defendant, or the defendant's defender raises objections to the victim's statement, witness testimony, or expert conclusion, and such victim's statement, witness testimony, or expert conclusion has a significant impact on conviction and sentencing; (2) Where the people's court considers that other persons should appear in court to testify. After being notified by the people's court according to law, victims, witnesses, and expert witnesses shall appear in court to testify; if a victim, witness, or expert witness does not appear in court, and their written statement, written testimony, or expert conclusion cannot be confirmed through cross-examination, such evidence shall not be used as the basis for deciding the case.

33. When hearing a case, the people's court shall pay attention to reviewing the legality of evidence. If there are leads or evidence indicating the possible existence of torture or other illegal evidence collection methods, the court shall conduct a careful review. When the people's court requests the people's procuratorate to submit relevant evidence, the people's procuratorate shall submit it within three days. If the people's procuratorate does not have the relevant materials, it shall explain the circumstances to the people's court.

34. When the court of first instance and the court of second instance hear a death penalty case, the collegial panel shall request the president to decide to submit the case to the adjudication committee for discussion. When the Supreme People's Court reviews a death penalty case, or when the higher people's court reviews a case of death penalty with a two-year reprieve, if the case is difficult or complex and the collegial panel considers it difficult to reach a decision, the panel shall request the president to decide to submit the case to the adjudication committee for discussion and decision. When the adjudication committee discusses a case, the chief procurator of the people's procuratorate at the same level, or a deputy chief procurator authorized by the chief procurator, may attend the meeting as a non-voting participant.

35. A People's Court shall render a judgment in accordance with the law based on the facts that have been ascertained through trial, the evidence, and relevant legal provisions. Where the case facts are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, and the defendant is found guilty according to law, a conviction shall be entered; where the defendant is found not guilty according to law, a verdict of not guilty shall be entered; where the evidence is insufficient and the defendant cannot be found guilty, a verdict of not guilty due to insufficient evidence and failure to establish the charged crime shall be entered; where the evidence for conviction is reliable but there are doubts regarding the evidence affecting sentencing, allowance shall be made at the time of sentencing.

36. The second instance People's Court shall promptly ascertain whether the defendant sentenced to death with immediate execution has retained defense counsel. Where no defense counsel has been retained, the court shall inform the defendant that he may retain defense counsel on his own or notify the legal aid institution to appoint a lawyer who undertakes the obligation of legal aid to provide defense for him. A People's Court shall notify the People's Procuratorate, the defendant, and his defense counsel to provide the list of witnesses and expert witnesses to testify in court five days before the court session, and shall serve the summons to the parties and the notices to defense counsel, witnesses, expert witnesses, and interpreters three days before the court session.

37. In the trial of a death penalty case at second instance, a court session shall be held in accordance with the law and relevant provisions. A People's Court shall notify the People's Procuratorate to review the case files ten days before the court session. The People's Procuratorate at the same level shall dispatch personnel to appear in court at the time specified in the notice from the People's Court.

38. After a second instance People's Court renders a judgment or ruling, if announced in court, the written judgment or ruling shall be served on the parties, defense counsel, and the People's Procuratorate at the same level within five days; if announced on a scheduled date, it shall be served immediately after the announcement.

39. In reviewing a death penalty case, a comprehensive review shall be conducted of the factual findings, application of law, and litigation procedures in the original trial judgment.

40. During the review of a death penalty case, if the defense counsel retained by the defendant requests to present opinions, the opinions of the defense counsel shall be heard, and a record shall be made and attached to the case file. If the defense counsel submits written opinions, they shall be attached to the case file.

41. In reviewing a death penalty case, the members of the collegial panel shall read the case files and submit written opinions for retention. Where there are doubts about the evidence, the evidence shall be investigated and verified, and if necessary, investigations shall be conducted at the crime scene.

42. When a High People's Court reviews a death penalty case, it shall interrogate the defendant. When the Supreme People's Court reviews a death penalty case, it shall, in principle, interrogate the defendant.

43. On the premise of ensuring the quality of case handling, a People's Court shall further improve the efficiency of handling death penalty review cases, and hear death penalty review cases fairly and promptly.

44. The People's Procuratorate shall, in accordance with the law, strengthen legal supervision over the handling of death penalty cases.

(V) Execution

45. When serving the written judgment approving the death penalty on the criminal, a People's Court shall inform the criminal that he has the right to apply to meet his close relatives. If the criminal applies to meet his close relatives and provides specific addresses and contact information, the People's Court shall grant the application; the original trial People's Court shall notify the close relatives of the criminal. If the close relatives of the criminal apply to meet him, the People's Court shall grant the application and promptly arrange the meeting.

46. Before delivering the criminal for execution of the death penalty, the first instance People's Court shall deliver the written judgment approving the death penalty to the People's Procuratorate at the same level, and notify the People's Procuratorate at the same level to dispatch personnel to supervise at the execution site three days before delivery.

47. If, before the execution of the death penalty, the first instance People's Court discovers any circumstance provided for in Article 211 of the Criminal Procedure Law, it shall suspend the execution and immediately report to the Supreme People's Court, which shall render a ruling. If the procuratorial personnel supervising the execution at the scene discover any circumstance provided for in Article 211 of the Criminal Procedure Law before the execution, they shall suggest that the People's Court suspend the execution.

48. The execution of a death penalty shall be made public. Parading the executed person through the streets or any other act that insults the personal dignity of the executed person is prohibited. Insulting the corpse is prohibited.

IV. Mutual Cooperation and Mutual Restraint Among the People's Court, People's Procuratorate, and Public Security Organ in Accordance with the Law

49. When handling death penalty cases, the People's Court, People's Procuratorate, and Public Security Organ shall earnestly implement the basic litigation principle of "division of responsibilities, mutual cooperation, and mutual restraint," and shall, based on the clear division of work provided by law, each perform its own duties and bear its own responsibilities, while also supporting each other and cooperating fully, to ensure the accurate and effective implementation of the law and jointly safeguard the quality of death penalty cases.

50. The People's Court, People's Procuratorate, and Public Security Organ shall, in accordance with the division of litigation functions and procedural settings, exercise mutual restraint to prevent errors or promptly correct errors, truly achieving neither wrongful conviction nor impunity, and neither unjust treatment nor leniency. Mutual restraint among the People's Court, People's Procuratorate, and Public Security Organ shall be reflected in the statutory litigation activities of each organ, and they shall not interfere with, intervene in, or resist the litigation activities of other organs in the lawful exercise of their powers in violation of procedures.

51. During the trial process, if it is discovered that the defendant may have statutory sentencing circumstances such as voluntary surrender or meritorious service, and supplementary evidence or supplementary investigation is needed, the People's Procuratorate shall suggest an adjournment of the trial. The period of adjournment shall not exceed one month. Where it is necessary to verify the defendant's disclosure of others' criminal acts, the People's Procuratorate may, in accordance with the nature of the crime, conduct the verification on its own according to law, or, if it falls under the jurisdiction of the Public Security Organ, may refer it to the Public Security Organ for verification. The People's Procuratorate shall promptly submit the verification results to the People's Court within the time limit prescribed by law.

V. Strict Implementation of the Accountability System for Case Handling

52. Where a person intentionally violates the provisions of the law and these Opinions, or due to serious irresponsibility, affects the quality of handling death penalty cases and causes serious consequences, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be subject to administrative sanctions or disciplinary sanctions by their unit or the competent authority at a higher level in accordance with relevant provisions; where the act constitutes a crime as in engaging in malpractices for personal gain or perverting the law, criminal liability shall be pursued according to law.
